title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus in women from northern provinces of Lao People’s Democratic Republic, 2018–2019
content:
by Vilaysone Khounvisith, Bounthome Samountry, Janko van Beek, Aurélie Sausy, Regina Brunnhoefer, Bounta Vongphachanh, Khamtim Samountry, Maude Pauly, Joel Mossong, Jessica Tapp, Claude P. Muller, Antony P. Black, Judith M. Hübschen

Background

Cervical cancer is a frequent cause of morbidity and mortality in women worldwide and strongly linked to the presence of high-risk (HR) human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes. The present study aimed to determine HPV prevalence and genotypes and their relationship with cytology results in Lao women.

Methods

Between October 2018 and February 2019, a total of 1302 asymptomatic women (mean age 37.4 years, range 18–76) from Xiengkhouang, Luangprabang, Oudomxay and Huaphan provinces were invited to answer a questionnaire, and cervical cells were collected for cytology and a swab for PCR and AnyplexTM II HPV-HR detection.

Results

Overall, 114 of 1268 women with evaluable samples (9.0%) had abnormal cytology and three (0.2%) had cervical cancer. AnyplexTM II HPV-HR kit detected 256 positives among 1184 participants (21.6%), with types 52, 58 and 16 being the most prevalent HR genotypes (20.4%, 12.8% and 11.7%, respectively). Multivariable analysis showed that participants aged ≥ 40 years (OR: 1.6; 95% CI: 1.1–2.4, p = 0.015) and those living in Luangprabang province (OR: 1.9; 95% CI: 1.1–3.2, p = 0.02) had a higher likelihood of abnormal cytology compared to younger women and those residing in Huaphan. Single/divorced/widow women had a higher probability of HPV detection compared to married women (OR: 2.3; 95% CI: 1.5–3.7, p < 0.001).

Conclusions

HPV 52, 58 and 16 were the most prevalent high-risk genotypes, clearly advocating for the introduction of the nonavalent vaccine. Periodic screening of women too old to benefit from the recently introduced vaccine should be considered.
